pageCache.text:
Vision & Ethos
"SHOW BY A GOOD LIFE THAT YOUR WORKS ARE DONE BY GENTLENESS BORN OF WISDOM"
SMMA is a Church school that serves our whole community. We aim to inspire and nurture young people to be happy and successful, to live well together, to become high achievers, to make a contribution to their local, national, and international communities, and to discover their vocation in our global society.
Our Ethos
Our school motto is at the heart of how we work and learn together in the Academy:
We believe that kindness, self-respect, tolerance, and respect for our learning environment are fundamental to who we are, they sit at the heart of the Academy’s ethos and are an important aspect of our ongoing mission to maintain a happy and successful community.

pageCache.pageTitle: Collective Worship - St Mary Magdalene Academy
pageCache.text:
Collective Worship
You can submit prayers and intentions to be added to our school prayer tree here
If you would like Fr Sam to pray for a private intention you can contact him here.
First thing in the morning, the whole school gathers together for a daily act of worship in our hall. While our collective worship is Christian in its basis, we ensure that our whole community feel welcome to be able to participate. Pupils throughout the school are encouraged to share prayers and intentions by noting them down in our prayer corner in the school library. We regularly visit our local churches for services throughout the year as a school and individual classes.
Year 6 take on the responsibility to set up the hall for our assemblies, putting out chairs and benches, setting up our reflection table and light our candle to signify the start of our worship. Each day of the week has a particular style to it. In our weekly newsletters, we share the theme of each assembly so those at home can continue conversations if they wish.
Monday is our celebration assembly. Each teacher presents three or four children with a certificate and tells the school why they are celebrating them that week. It is a great way to start our week; reflecting on the successes of the previous one. During this assembly, our Year 6 House Captains update the school with the latest house points and any child or adult who has a birthday that week is presented with a certificate and is sung to. This is the day any other prizes and notable achievements are shared with the school.
Tuesday's assembly is led by our Chaplain, Fr. Sam. He guides us in learning about stories from the Bible and the Christian tradition, encouraging us to reflect on how these teachings impact our lives both as individuals and as a school community.
Wednesday's assembly is led by our Head of Primary or Deputy Head. During this assembly, we might reflect on one of our school values, think about a local, national or global event, and learn about another culture.
Thursday is our singing assembly. We love to sing at SMMA and our music teacher knows how to bring us together in harmony.
Friday's assembly is often a class assembly. This is when the whole community is invited to watch a class share their learning. This is an enjoyable way for parents/carers, families, staff and pupils to end the week and is always well attended. If there is no class assembly, the assembly will be led by the Head of Primary or Deputy Head and will follow the same format as Wednesday assemblies.
Our collective worship policy can be found here collective-worship.pdf.

Y7 Welcome Evening 2026
Y7 Welcome Evening Information 2026
I hope your child had a good day with us today and that they are looking forward to the term ahead.
I am writing to invite you to our Year 7 Welcome Evening on Thursday 10 September from 6pm – 7pm.
The evening will consist of a 30-minute reception- a chance to socialise with other parents and staff while enjoying some refreshments. At 6.30 there will be a talk which will include a great deal of important information about the year ahead.
Due to the capacity of the venue, we are unable to accommodate anyone other than the parent/carers; please do not bring your Year 7 child or any younger/older siblings.
For catering and organisation, we ask that you complete a simple form confirming your attendance. The form can be accessed by clicking here and scrolling to the bottom of the page.
I look forward to seeing you next Thursday.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to SMMA - St Mary Magdalene Academy
pageCache.text:
Welcome to SMMA
St Mary Magdalene Academy is part of Hive Education Trust and sponsored by the London Diocesan Board for Schools. It is a Christian community of learning which aims to nurture young people to become high achievers and to discover their vocation in a global society. We welcome pupils and students from all faiths and none to our schools, which strive to be inspirational communities of learning focused on happy, successful children.
Our motto is: Show by a good life that your works are done by gentleness born of wisdom (James 3:13).
The motto succinctly captures our aspirations and our focus on developing a set of values that will allow our young people to grow into contributory citizens in our local, national, and global community. Our core values of Trust, Compassion, Forgiveness, Integrity, Resilience, and Thankfulness clearly come from our Christian foundation but are appropriate to a life lived well in any community.
We have come to recognise that with the right level of commitment, the impossible can be achieved very quickly; it’s only miracles that take a little longer! We expect that commitment to achieving the impossible from staff, pupils, older students, and parents. Our experience tells us it can be done if the desire is great enough.
Our approach can best be summed up by the words of Nelson Mandela:
Education is the great engine of personal development. It is through education that the daughter of a peasant can become a doctor, that a son of a mineworker can become the head of the mine, that a child of farm workers can become the president of a great nation. It is what we make out of what we have, not what we are given that separates one person from another.
Vicky Linsley, Trust CEO
Any requests for copies of policies should be made to firstcontact@smmacademy.org or at Reception.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to the Primary School - St Mary Magdalene Academy
pageCache.text:
Welcome to the Primary School
"Everyone knows everyone in this small, friendly school with different year groups playing together and parents who are involved. A really solid, well-planned education with plenty of extracurricular clubs and activities, creating articulate, thinking pupils who have been listened to and encouraged to engage in, and have meaningful conversations about, all their learning." Good Schools Guide
St Mary Magdalene Academy includes a one form entry Primary for children ages 4 to 11. Situated in a modern building, but with a long history, the Primary is a happy and ambitious place to learn and work.
We have high aspirations for all pupils at the Academy. Our governors, staff, families, and pupils all strive towards our core purpose: ensuring our pupils are happy and successful.
We take great pride in the arrangement of our curriculum, the foundations of which are built on embedding core knowledge in literacy and mathematics. A carefully structured curriculum ensures that our pupils attain the highest standards, leaving Year 6 with both strong attainment and progress from their starting points.
A strength of the Primary is the breadth of our curriculum. Our wider curriculum provides a structured and depth approach that delivers a challenging, broad and balanced curriculum. As a church Academy, we are committed to providing high-quality religious education. Furthermore, specialist teachers, often from the Secondary, work throughout the key stages to deliver Music, Physical Education, and Mandarin.
A vast variety of rich opportunities in which children participate are planned throughout their time at the school. These include a range of extra-curricular clubs, assemblies, trips (which take advantage of our location in London), and overnight residential excursions, and the chance to perform in our fantastic annual Shakespeare performance. A quick glance through our newsletter archive will give you a flavour of the extended curriculum we offer.
A real sense of community is shared by all at our school. Staff work together to improve teaching and learning and build strong relationships with families based on mutual support and trust. We are also very fortunate to be supported by an excellent and inclusive PTSA.
High-quality education can be a great equalising force in our society; it empowers people and is a key ingredient for their success. We are dedicated to providing a rich and welcoming environment so that all our pupils flourish.
We welcome visitors and look forward to showing you our school.
Kate Dingle Primary Headteacher

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to the Secondary School - St Mary Magdalene Academy
pageCache.text:
Welcome to the Secondary School
Pupils are very proud of their school. They describe it as a kind and welcoming place that promotes a keen sense of family, community and inclusion. Ofsted Full Inspection
The Academy’s ambitious curriculum features academic and creative development with a global outlook. SIAMS Full Inspection
At St Mary Magdalene Academy, we aim to nurture young people to become high achievers and to discover their vocation in a global society. We have a strong focus on getting to know each child individually, pushing them to achieve their personal best whilst also ensuring that they become well-rounded, responsible citizens. The school motto, show by a good life that your works are done by gentleness born of wisdom, taken from James’ book of the Bible lies at the core of our values. Fundamentally, it is about being decent people. The Academy's strap-line’ is Happy and Successful. We focus on ensuring that pupils are happy in school, that they feel part of the family, so they are able to flourish and be successful. As part of ensuring that pupils are happy, we have a House system with ‘Family Groups’ and a ‘Guardian’ with only about 20 pupils within each group. The impact of that, knowing each other positively and supportively, is significant as pupils move around the building or use the play spaces. Our curriculum offer is broad and balanced, ensuring that pupils have access to a range of different subjects. In the Lower School, pupils are taught the ISEB (Independent School Exam Board) curriculum, which ensures the pupils are well challenged and prepared for the academic journey ahead. In the Upper School, pupils work towards nine GCSEs with the possibility of some pupils doing more with courses in Astronomy, Further Maths and extra languages available to those interested. At Sixth Form, we have an academically selective offer for pupils to study A Levels with the view that they will then head off to top universities or higher-level apprenticeships. Outside of the classroom, we have a broad extracurricular offer in music, drama, and sport, with clubs ranging from the Debate Club to the Acting Academy, all the way to the Dungeons and Dragons Society. As well as this, pupils can sign up to Masterclasses, which are inspiring talks or workshops delivered by a range of successful individuals, from Permanent Secretaries, Nobel Prize winners, to Booker Prize-winning authors. All of these experiences ensure that the pupils leave the Academy as ambitious, talented and well-rounded individuals.
John Reardon Secondary Headteacher
When the Good Schools Guide visited us. They said “A shining example of an excellent school. Parents and pupils are aware they have picked the golden ticket if they can get an education here – the results are evidence of top quality teaching, and the children’s involvement and happiness are enhanced by the wide enrichment programme, whilst the pastoral care provides a tight safety net. If you want a top-notch inclusive comprehensive education, this is the place to go.”
Please click the Goods Schools Guide icon to read the full report.

pageCache.pageTitle: Welcome to St Mary Magdalene Sixth Form - St Mary Magdalene Academy
pageCache.text:
Welcome to St Mary Magdalene Sixth Form
To apply for a place in our sixth form for September 2027 entry.
CLICK HERE to complete the application form before january 31 2027.
“One of the Top 5 highest rated sixth forms in England.”
Choosing your Sixth Form is one of the biggest steps on the road to adulthood. In the next two years, you’ll be making huge leaps forward – not just in your studies, but in your life skills as well. You’ll be gaining confidence, making choices, and enjoying new friendships that will set the tone of your adult life.
You may already know where – or what – you want to be in life. Great. We can help you get there. But if you’re still thinking about it, that’s ok too. We’d like to be part of this giant step with you.
At St Mary Magdalene Academy Sixth Form, we’re confident we can bring out the best in you. We’ll treat you like an adult, guide you at every step, help you achieve your best results, and make sure you enjoy your time here too.
"The teachers really keep me motivated, encouraging me to identify and work on my own strengths."
And it’s not just talk. We’ll back it up with a three-point promise to you. Now please read on...
1. We promise to help you achieve your full potential.
Last year’s Sixth Form exam results at St Mary Magdalene were our best ever. With small class sizes, the highest quality teaching, and a personal approach, we can bring out the very best in you.
"The Academy has enabled me to challenge myself, and pushed me to new heights."
Find out more here: Sixth Form exam resultsA full range of A LevelsSixth Form teaching and study support
2. We promise to give you the life skills to succeed.
It’s not just about exam results anymore. Every employer or university wants to see the real person behind the results: to find out about you.
Through our network of partners in the UK and overseas, we’ll give you the opportunities and space to develop as an individual – and to create a Personal Statement that will impress.
We promise to take you to see at least one university while you’re in Sixth Form. And we’ll guarantee you a work placement within one of our partner companies.
Our ‘Masterclass’ talks programme will fire your enthusiasm and help you decide where you want to go in life. And our careers coaching will set you safely on your way.
"When I leave I want to be a cinematographer. My teachers are helping by showing me options on how to get into film."
"I want to study Law at King’s College. My teachers’ constructive advice is improving my chances of getting there."
University and Careers CoachingCreating a Personal Statement to Impress The Journey to Independence
3. We promise it won’t be just hard work.
Hard work is important, for sure. But it’s important to enjoy your time here too. Our friendly Sixth Form will help you settle in. And with a free gym membership, free wi–fi, great friends, and amazing activities and trips to enjoy, you’ll have two years to remember… forever!
But don’t just take our word for it.
"The students we met were gorgeous – a memorably impressive bunch!"
The good schools guide
There's our students’ words, our parents’ words, and Ofsted’s words. Or The Independent’s words. Or the Daily Telegraph’s words. Or The Good Schools Guide’s words... But best of all, please come and judge for yourself why we're rated 'one of the top 5 Sixth Forms in England'.
We’d love to meet you. Just email us to arrange a visit.
"The atmosphere is welcoming and family–like, but at the same time serious and inspiring."
"The international environment has helped me make friends from all over the world."

pageCache.pageTitle: Partnership with Parents - St Mary Magdalene Academy
pageCache.text:
Partnership with Parents
At SMMA Primary we want to work in partnership with the parents of our pupils. Partnership starts with good communication. Here are a few of the ways we stay in touch with the parents at school.
Senior leader on the gate at the beginning and end of the school day
We want our school leaders to be accessible for parents to be able to ask questions, offer suggestions and share concerns.
Teaching staff in the playground at the end of the school day
Children are collected and dropped off in the playground. Teachers will stay out in the playground at the end of the day so you can pass on any messages. You may also contact the school office to book a meeting with a teacher.
Each pupil has their own personal planner which is used as a reading record and for notes between school and home.
We will send you reminders about events coming up
The weekly newsletter is full of important information and diary dates so do check this each week.
Specific letters will go out for different events. Look out for these in book bags.
These are held midway through the Autumn and Spring terms.
Meet the teacher events
At the beginning of the school year, we invite parents to an after-school meeting to meet the new class teacher and find out more about the curriculum and routines.
We host a variety of workshops throughout the year.
We recognise that for some parents it is challenging to meet with teachers and senior leaders in person or over the telephone due to work. Staff are happy to communicate via email in this case.
How can I support my child's education?
Parental engagement with school and education can encompass a number of different things and different ways. If parents are unable to be in school it does not mean that they are still not providing vital support. Below are some of the different ways parents can be involved.
Parental involvement with the school
Coming on school trips; attending school events; coming to Parents' Evenings
Parental involvement with children's schooling
Helping with home learning
Parental engagement with children's learning
Moral support; discussing learning at home; demonstrating a positive attitude towards learning
At SMMA Primary we value the support of parents and carers - we know that by working together we can ensure the best for your child. However, we do understand that sometimes issues may arise. Just as we have the SMMA Way for pupils, we also have a Code of Conduct for parents and carers which we expect all to adhere to. It also includes some answers to some questions parents and carers who are new may have.
Parent and carer code of conduct Primary.pdf
Please also see our Home-School agreement, which outlines the responsibilities of the school, the pupil and the parent/carer to ensure the mutual goal of providing the best possible school environment and social, emotional and academic success for all pupils.

pageCache.pageTitle: Record-Breaking A Level Results for SMMA Sixth Form Students - News - St Mary Magdalene Academy
pageCache.text:
News
Record-Breaking A Level Results for SMMA Sixth Form Students
We are delighted to congratulate our St Mary Magdalene Academy Sixth Form students as they celebrate an outstanding set of A Level results.
This year, 43% of all grades awarded were A or A*, reflecting another year of exceptional academic achievement across the Sixth Form. These results continue the Academy's strong record of success, with students progressing to some of the leading universities and institutions in the country, alongside an exciting range of other destinations.
"It is a real privilege to see this remarkable group of young people reach such an important milestone. Throughout their time in the Sixth Form, they have contributed so much to the life of the Academy and their ambition and determination have been remarkable. I am delighted to see so many now progressing to some of the very best institutions, and I know they leave us well prepared for happy and successful futures. I would also like to thank their parents and carers, whose encouragement and support have been so important throughout their time with us. We are incredibly proud of everything this cohort has achieved and wish them every success in the years ahead."
"The top grades at A Level are a very high bar indeed and I am immensely proud of the students and teachers of St Mary Magdalene Academy Sixth Form who worked so hard to achieve these excellent results."
"Another fantastic year for the students of SMMA! We are extremely proud of their achievements and it is testament to the hard work they put in. A huge thank you also to the Sixth Form team and teachers, whose relentless effort and support have helped our students achieve such wonderful results. Wishing the students all the very best for their next steps!"
Please read on for some of the many outstanding achievements and destinations of this year's leavers:

pageCache.pageTitle: OUTSTANDING 2026 GCSE Results For SMMA Students - News - St Mary Magdalene Academy
pageCache.text:
News
OUTSTANDING 2026 GCSE Results For SMMA Students
This year’s GCSE results are another set of fantastic outcomes for the pupils of St Mary Magdalene Academy.
For the second year running, over 45% of all grades were 7 (the old A grade) or above - a remarkable achievement that opens the door to Key Stage 5 courses with the most demanding entry requirements.
We are also delighted that over 70% of pupils achieved a strong pass (grade 5 or above) in both English and Maths, with more than 80% securing at least a standard pass (grade 4, equivalent to the old C) in these core subjects. These results reflect the pupils’ tremendous commitment, hard work and perseverance throughout their studies.
Across the wider curriculum, there were outstanding subject results. 100% of pupils achieved grades 4–9 in Astronomy, Biology, Chemistry, Design and Technology, German, Italian, Mandarin, Music and Physics, and in all of these subjects more than 60% attained grade 7 or higher.
There were so many individual successes that we have selected just a few to highlight: Aliénor, Daniel, Leo, Max, Maria, Oscar and Rosalie all got seven or more Grade 9s across their subjects; Arian, Tom and Nina achieved the coveted “9 at 9”; special mentions for Maddie, Ornaith and Lucy who achieved ten grade 9s and Yasmina and Esmie who secured eleven grade 9s - an extraordinary achievement.
We are immensely proud of all our pupils and their achievements, and congratulate them on the dedication and determination that have made these results possible.
Director of Curriculum, Dr Claire Bisdorff, says:
‘We are delighted to celebrate the outstanding GCSE achievements of our 2026 cohort. The results are a reflection of the resilience, determination and commitment pupils have shown throughout their time with us, and we are incredibly proud of everything they have accomplished. As they take their next steps in education, we are confident that the skills, knowledge and confidence they have developed will help them to thrive.
We would also like to recognise the dedication of our teaching staff, whose encouragement, expertise and unwavering support have played a crucial part in helping our pupils reach their potential.’
Secondary Headteacher, John Reardon says:
'The Class of 2026 have achieved an exceptional set of results, and we are incredibly proud of them.
Their success is a reflection of their hard work, commitment and determination, from early-morning study to extra sessions after school. Above all, this year group has been wonderful to work with; the pupils have been kind and gentle throughout their time at the Academy. We wish them every success for their next steps!
A final great big thank you to all of my colleagues who have challenged and supported these pupils along the way.'
Trust CEO, Vicky Linsley says:
'SMMA continues to be a fantastic school, turning out consistently outstanding results so far above the national average year after year. That is a remarkable achievement in a truly comprehensive school. Congratulations!'
